domain: 64-bit scalar integer-to-pointer constant-expression casts, including zero and nonzero; global-address pointer constants. FP/vector casts separately excluded from scalar scope.
reason: Integer-to-pointer constant folding produces a ConstantExpr/pointer-address constant, whose syntax is absent from VeIR. For nonpoison input the operational inttoptr result is memory-dependent through objectOfAddress, whereas Puddle InterpretsTo requires one memory-uniform result; even integer-zero does not uniformly encode the distinguished null pointer for arbitrary MemoryState. Global-address constant folding also has no local memory/symbol certificate. No identity re-creation or vacuous pure proof is counted.

domain: 64-bit pointer-to-integer-to-pointer and integer-to-pointer-to-integer cast-pair variants; pointer provenance/object identity and memory-dependent decoding.
reason: Pointer/integer cast-pair cancellation cannot be faithfully expressed using the current pure local InterpretsTo judgment: inttoptr depends on memory.decode/objectOfAddress, but InterpretsTo demands the same intermediate result for every memory. Checked operational witnesses show integer1 decodes to pointer object0/address1 in empty memory and object1/address1 in witnessMemory; ptrtoint of object1/address1 loses its object identifier. This is a model correspondence limitation, not an LLVM bug or a false Pattern.Valid witness. Neither direction is counted using vacuity.
